questions.question: What are the three levels of HR Manager structure?
questions.solution_html:
• The three general levels in the HR manager structure are:
  • a. Operational/Specialist Level: Focuses on daily tasks like recruitment, payroll, and
  • administration.
  • b. Manager/Generalist Level: Oversees teams, manages employee relations, and
  • implements policies.
  • c. Strategic/Executive Level (HR Director/CHRO): Aligns HR strategy with overall
  • business goals and organizational change.

questions.question: What is evaluation stage in ADDIE?
questions.solution_html:
• The Evaluation stage is the ﬁnal phase of the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design,
  • Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) of instructional design. The purpose of
  • the Evaluation stage is to measure the e Ưectiveness and e Ưiciency of the entire
  • instructional program and determine if the learning objectives set in the Analysis phase
  • were met.

questions.question: Define grievance procedure.
questions.solution_html:
• A grievance procedure is a formal, documented process that an employer establishes
  • to manage, investigate, and resolve complaints (grievances) raised by an employee
  • about their working conditions, treatment, or relationship with management or
  • colleagues.

questions.question: Differentiate between job description and job specification with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• A Job Description is a document that focuses on the job itself, detailing the speciﬁc
  • duties, responsibilities, and working conditions of the role. In contrast, the Job
  • Speciﬁcation focuses on the ideal candidate, outlining the necessary skills,
  • qualiﬁcations, education, and experience required for a person to successfully perform
  • those duties.

questions.question: Explain the role of skill and performance in pay determination.
questions.solution_html:
• Skill-based pay rewards an employee for the capabilities and knowledge they possess
  • and acquire, driving continuous learning. Performance-based pay, however, rewards
  • employees for achieving measurable results and high output in their current role.
  • Together, they create a ﬂexible system that rewards both potential (skills) and proven
  • contribution (performance).

questions.question: What are the benefits and limitations of job description in modern organizations?
questions.solution_html:
• Job descriptions (JDs) beneﬁt modern organizations by providing clarity on roles,
  • streamlining recruitment, and setting the basis for performance management.
  • However, their limitations include rigidity, making them quickly outdated in fast-paced
  • environments, and potentially stiﬂing employee creativity or willingness to take on new
  • tasks outside the deﬁned scope.
